page: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an instance type within the inf1 family, designated as AWS Inferentia Gen1 xlarge. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, which yields 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is not included, meaning the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage, while baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest CPU and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng performance and single-threaded gzip compression fall into the average tier, with gzip compression reaching 25.33 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3929.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2526.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read and write speeds measured at 27.68 GB/sec and 23.83 GB/sec respectively, placing them in the lower performance brackets. For lightweight language model tasks, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 75.74 tokens/second on a small 135M model, though prompt processing is weaker at 225.83 tokens/second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inf1.xlarge offers an entry-level hardware profile with dedicated compute resources, making it a budget-conscious option for workloads that do not require high memory density or local storage. Given its hardware constraints and benchmark results, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded utility tasks, or small-scale machine learning inference workloads that fit within its 8 GB memory capacity.
